sections.heading: COLOR ENCODING PICKING
sections.content:
ProBuilder implements offscreen GPU element picking by rendering unique color-encoded identifiers for faces, vertices, and edges into an offscreen `RenderTexture` (lookup texture), reading back pixel buffers to the CPU, and decoding the pixel colors into references to specific mesh elements.

1. Color Encoding and Decoding Algorithms:
- Element identifiers are 32-bit unsigned integers (`uint`), where the lower 24 bits store the unique index and the highest byte is reserved. Encoded colors are stored in 32-bit RGBA structures (`Color32`) with alpha fixed to 255 (`0xFF`).
- Bit-packing considers host architecture endianness via `System.BitConverter.IsLittleEndian`:
  - Little-Endian Encoding (`EncodeRGBA`):
    - Red: `(byte)(hash >> 16 & 0xFF)`
    - Green: `(byte)(hash >> 8 & 0xFF)`
    - Blue: `(byte)(hash & 0xFF)`
    - Alpha: `255`
  - Big-Endian Encoding (`EncodeRGBA`):
    - Red: `(byte)(hash >> 24 & 0xFF)`
    - Green: `(byte)(hash >> 16 & 0xFF)`
    - Blue: `(byte)(hash >> 8 & 0xFF)`
    - Alpha: `255`
  - Little-Endian Decoding (`DecodeRGBA`):
    - `return (uint)color.r << 16 | (uint)color.g << 8 | (uint)color.b;`
  - Big-Endian Decoding (`DecodeRGBA`):
    - `return (uint)color.r << 24 | (uint)color.g << 16 | (uint)color.b << 8;`
- Reserved Hash Values in `SelectionPickerRenderer`:
  - `k_PickerHashNone = 0x00`: Indicates no hit / background clear color / black occlusion mask.
  - `k_PickerHashMin = 0x1`: Lowest valid hash index.
  - `k_PickerHashMax = 0x00FFFFFF`: Background clear white color (`0xFFFFFF`).
  - `k_MinEdgePixelsForValidSelection = 1`: Minimum threshold of edge pixels required to register an edge selection.

2. Face Picking Geometry Generation (`GenerateFacePickingObjects`):
- Takes `IList<ProBuilderMesh> selection` and allocates `GameObject[] pickerObjects` and `Dictionary<uint, (ProBuilderMesh, Face)> map`.
- Index starts at `uint index = 0`.
- For each `ProBuilderMesh pb` in `selection`:
  - Instantiates temporary `Mesh m`.
  - Sets `m.vertices = pb.positionsInternal` and `m.triangles = pb.facesInternal.SelectMany(x => x.indexesInternal).ToArray()`.
  - Allocates `Color32[] colors = new Color32[m.vertexCount]`.
  - For each `Face f` in `pb.facesInternal`:
    - Computes `Color32 color = EncodeRGBA(index++)`.
    - Adds lookup entry mapping `DecodeRGBA(color)` to pair `(pb, f)` in `map`.
    - Assigns `colors[f.distinctIndexesInternal[n]] = color` for all distinct indices in the face.
  - Assigns `m.colors32 = colors`.
  - Creates a temporary `GameObject` via `InternalUtility.MeshGameObjectWithTransform(pb.name + " (Face Depth Test)", pb.transform, m, BuiltinMaterials.facePickerMaterial, true)`.
  - Sets `BuiltinMaterials.facePickerMaterial.SetColor("_Tint", Color.white)` (`k_Whitef`).

3. Vertex Picking Geometry Generation (`GenerateVertexPickingObjects` and `BuildVertexMesh`):
- Vertex picking uses screen-facing billboard quads for each shared vertex group.
- Index starts at `uint index = 0x02` to avoid `0x00` (black occlusion mask) and `0x01`.
- Length is clamped to `Math.Min(pb.sharedVerticesInternal.Length, ushort.MaxValue / 4 - 1)` (maximum 16382 quads) due to 16-bit mesh index limits.
- For each shared vertex index `i`:
  - Position `v = pb.positionsInternal[pb.sharedVerticesInternal[i][0]]`.
  - 4 vertices placed at `v` in `t_billboards`.
  - Quad UVs: `(0,0)`, `(1,0)`, `(0,1)`, `(1,1)` in `t_uvs`.
  - Billboard vertex offsets: `-up - right`, `-up + right`, `up - right`, `up + right` in `t_uv2`.
  - Triangles: two triangles `(0,1,2)` and `(1,3,2)` per quad in `t_tris`.
  - Encodes `Color32 color = EncodeRGBA(index)` and registers mapping of `index++` to `(pb, i)` in `map`.
  - Assigns `color` to all 4 quad vertices in `t_col`.
- Creates temporary `GameObject` with `BuiltinMaterials.vertexPickerMaterial`.
- When `doDepthTest == true`, instantiates duplicate depth mask GameObjects with `pb.mesh` and `BuiltinMaterials.facePickerMaterial` with `_Tint` set to `Color.black` (`k_Blackf`).

4. Edge Picking Geometry Generation (`GenerateEdgePickingObjects` and `BuildEdgeMesh`):
- Line mesh generation starts at `uint index = 0x2`.
- Counts total edges across faces, clamped to `Math.Min(edgeCount, ushort.MaxValue / 2 - 1)`.
- Allocates `Vector3[] positions` and `Color32[] color` of length `elementCount * 2`.
- For each edge in each face:
  - `positions[positionIndex + 0] = pb.positionsInternal[edge.a]`
  - `positions[positionIndex + 1] = pb.positionsInternal[edge.b]`
  - Encodes `Color32 c = EncodeRGBA(index)` and registers mapping of `index++` to `(pb, edge)` in `map`.
  - `color[positionIndex + 0] = c` and `color[positionIndex + 1] = c`.
  - `tris[positionIndex + 0] = positionIndex + 0` and `tris[positionIndex + 1] = positionIndex + 1`.
- Sets mesh topology to `MeshTopology.Lines` via `mesh.SetIndices(tris, MeshTopology.Lines, 0)`.
- Creates temporary `GameObject` with `BuiltinMaterials.edgePickerMaterial`.
- If `doDepthTest == true`, also creates depth mask GameObjects with `BuiltinMaterials.facePickerMaterial` and `_Tint = Color.black`.

5. Offscreen Render and Cleanup Lifecycle:
- `pickerRenderer.RenderLookupTexture(camera, BuiltinMaterials.selectionPickerShader, "ProBuilderPicker", width, height)` executes rendering.
- All generated temporary GameObjects and shared meshes are destroyed via `UObject.DestroyImmediate`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, color-encoded picking can be implemented using a dedicated SubViewport set to UPDATE_ONCE with an integer color format (RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R32_UINT or RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM) or an unshaded spatial shader writing encoded index IDs to ALBEDO. Alternatively, CPU-side GPU compute dispatch with RenderingDevice can read back the buffer without stalling the main rendering thread.

sections.heading: RECT SELECTION
sections.content:
ProBuilder supports box/drag selection of vertices, faces, and edges through `SelectionPicker` and `SelectionPickerRenderer`. Selection behavior is configured via `PickerOptions`, which contains `depthTest` (`bool`) and `rectSelectMode` (`RectSelectMode.Partial` versus `RectSelectMode.Complete`).

1. Coordinate Space Transformation:
- `rect` is supplied in GUI space coordinates where `(0, 0)` is the top-left corner of the camera viewport and coordinates span `[0..width, 0..height]`.
- When reading pixels from the bottom-left origin texture buffer, `SelectionPickerRenderer` transforms the bounds:
  - `int ox = Math.Max(0, Mathf.FloorToInt(pickerRect.x));`
  - `int oy = Math.Max(0, Mathf.FloorToInt((tex.height - pickerRect.y) - pickerRect.height));`
  - `int width = Mathf.FloorToInt(pickerRect.width);`
  - `int height = Mathf.FloorToInt(pickerRect.height);`

2. Face Rectangle Selection (`SelectionPicker.PickFacesInRect`):
- Partial Mode with Depth Testing (`options.depthTest == true && options.rectSelectMode == RectSelectMode.Partial`):
  - Delegates to `SelectionPickerRenderer.PickFacesInRect(cam, rect, selectable, width, height)`.
  - Renders face color lookup texture.
  - Retrieves raw pixel array `Color32[] pix = tex.GetPixels32()`.
  - Iterates rows `y` from `oy` to `Min(oy + height, imageHeight)` and columns `x` from `ox` to `Min(ox + width, imageWidth)`.
  - Decodes `uint v = SelectionPickerRenderer.DecodeRGBA(pix[y * imageWidth + x])`.
  - Maintains `HashSet<uint> used` to ensure unique lookups: if `used.Add(v)` and `map.TryGetValue(v, out hit)` succeed, appends `hit.item2` (`Face`) to `selected[hit.item1]`.
- Complete Mode or No Depth Testing:
  - Transforms all vertex positions to GUI space: `screenPoints[nn] = cam.ScreenToGuiPoint(cam.WorldToScreenPoint(trs.TransformPoint(positions[nn])), pixelsPerPoint)`.
  - Complete Mode (`options.rectSelectMode == RectSelectMode.Complete`):
    - Evaluates near clip clipping: `if (screenPoints[face.indexesInternal[0]].z < cam.nearClipPlane) continue;`.
    - Evaluates if first index is inside: `if (rect.Contains(screenPoints[face.indexesInternal[0]]))`.
    - Iterates remaining distinct indices `q = 1..face.distinctIndexesInternal.Length - 1`. If any index is behind `nearClipPlane` or outside `rect`, rejects the face.
    - If all vertices are enclosed, evaluates occlusion: `if (!options.depthTest || !HandleUtility.PointIsOccluded(cam, pb, trs.TransformPoint(Math.Average(positions, face.distinctIndexesInternal)))) selectedFaces.Add(face);`.
  - Partial Mode without Depth Testing (`options.rectSelectMode == RectSelectMode.Partial && !options.depthTest`):
    - Computes 2D bounding box `Bounds2D poly = new Bounds2D(screenPoints, face.edgesInternal)`.
    - If `poly.Intersects(rect)`:
      - Check A: If `rect` contains any polygon vertex with `p.z > cam.nearClipPlane`, marks `overlaps = true`.
      - Check B: If not, checks if the polygon contains any of the 4 `rect` corners (`tl`, `tr`, `bl`, `br`) using `Math.PointInPolygon(screenPoints, poly, face.edgesInternal, corner)`.
      - Check C: If not, tests 2D line segment intersection between all face edges and the 4 rectangle boundary segments using `Math.GetLineSegmentIntersect`.
      - If `overlaps == true`, adds face to selection.

3. Edge Rectangle Selection (`SelectionPicker.PickEdgesInRect`):
- Partial Mode with Depth Testing (`options.depthTest == true && options.rectSelectMode == RectSelectMode.Partial`):
  - Delegates to `SelectionPickerRenderer.PickEdgesInRect(cam, rect, selectable, true, width, height)`.
  - Renders edge line mesh and depth mask.
  - Accumulates hit counts per color identifier in `Dictionary<uint, uint> pixelCount`.
  - Requires `kvp.Value > k_MinEdgePixelsForValidSelection` (`k_MinEdgePixelsForValidSelection = 1`, requiring strictly 2 or more pixels) to reject subpixel edge false positives.
- Complete Mode or No Depth Testing:
  - Evaluates both edge endpoints `a` and `b` in GUI coordinates.
  - Complete Mode: skips if `a.z < cam.nearClipPlane || b.z < cam.nearClipPlane`. Verifies `rect.Contains(a) && rect.Contains(b)`. If `options.depthTest == true`, checks occlusion at the midpoint: `!HandleUtility.PointIsOccluded(cam, pb, (posA + posB) * 0.5f)`.
  - Partial Mode: tests 2D line clipping via `Math.RectIntersectsLineSegment(rect, a, b)`.

4. Vertex Rectangle Selection (`SelectionPicker.PickVerticesInRect`):
- Depth Testing (`options.depthTest == true`):
  - Delegates to `SelectionPickerRenderer.PickVerticesInRect`.
  - Scans pixels in `pickerRect`, decodes IDs, maps to `(ProBuilderMesh, int sharedIndex)`.
  - Post-processing for coincident vertices: iterates selected shared vertex indices, computes `VectorHash.GetHashCode(positions[sharedVertices[x][0]])`, and selects all shared vertices in the mesh sharing identical spatial coordinates.
- No Depth Testing (`options.depthTest == false`):
  - Bypasses GPU rendering for speed. Iterates `pb.sharedVerticesInternal`, transforms `positions[sharedIndexes[n][0]]` to screen coordinates, clips `p.z < cam.nearClipPlane`, scales by `pixelsPerPoint`, and tests `rect.Contains(p)`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, drag rectangle selection can be implemented on CPU for Complete mode and non-depth-tested Partial mode using Camera3D.unproject_position() and Geometry2D.is_point_in_polygon() / Geometry2D.segment_intersects_segment(). For depth-tested Partial mode, rendering an integer picking texture into a SubViewport and performing a rectangular CPU pixel read via Image.get_data() mirrors ProBuilder's exact logic.

sections.heading: CLICK SELECTION
sections.content:
Single-click element selection in ProBuilder is performed via direct geometric raycasting using `SelectionPicker.PickFace` and `HandleUtility.FaceRaycast`.

1. Single Click Face Picking (`SelectionPicker.PickFace`):
- Constructs a world ray from the screen click position: `Ray ray = camera.ScreenPointToRay(mousePosition)`.
- Calls `HandleUtility.FaceRaycast(ray, pickable, out hit, Mathf.Infinity, CullingMode.Back)`.
- If the ray hits a face, retrieves and returns `pickable.facesInternal[hit.face]`; otherwise returns `null`.

2. RaycastHit Data Structure (`RaycastHit`):
- `float distance`: Ray distance from origin to intersection point in model units.
- `Vector3 point`: Hit coordinate in model space.
- `Vector3 normal`: Surface normal vector of the intersected triangle.
- `int face`: Zero-based index of the hit `Face` in `ProBuilderMesh.facesInternal`.

3. Raycast Algorithm (`HandleUtility.FaceRaycast`):
- Step 1: Transforms world ray into mesh model space:
  - `worldRay.origin -= mesh.transform.position;`
  - `worldRay.origin = mesh.transform.worldToLocalMatrix * worldRay.origin;`
  - `worldRay.direction = mesh.transform.worldToLocalMatrix * worldRay.direction;`
- Step 2: Iterates over all faces `i = 0..faces.Length - 1` (skipping any face in `HashSet<Face> ignore`).
- Step 3: Iterates triangle triplets `j = 0; j < indexes.Length; j += 3`:
  - `a = positions[indexes[j + 0]]`, `b = positions[indexes[j + 1]]`, `c = positions[indexes[j + 2]]`.
  - Computes unnormalized surface normal: `Vector3 nrm = Vector3.Cross(b - a, c - a)`.
  - Computes dot product with ray direction: `float dot = Vector3.Dot(worldRay.direction, nrm)`.
  - Culling check:
    - `CullingMode.Front`: Skip if `dot < 0f` (culled front-facing).
    - `CullingMode.Back`: Skip if `dot > 0f` (culled back-facing).
    - `CullingMode.None`: Do not skip.
  - Tests ray-triangle intersection via `Math.RayIntersectsTriangle(worldRay, a, b, c, out dist, out point)` (Möller-Trumbore algorithm calculating determinant `det = Vector3.Dot(e1, Vector3.Cross(dir, e2))` and barycentric coordinates `u` and `v`).
  - If hit occurs and `dist < OutHitPoint` and `dist <= distance`:
    - Updates `OutHitPoint = dist`, `OutHitFace = i`, `OutNrm = nrm`.
- Step 4: Instantiates `hit = new RaycastHit(OutHitPoint, worldRay.GetPoint(OutHitPoint), OutNrm, OutHitFace)` and returns `OutHitFace > -1`.

4. Dual Cull Mode Raycasting (`HandleUtility.FaceRaycastBothCullModes`):
- Raycasts against both front-facing (`CullingMode.Back`) and back-facing (`CullingMode.Front`) triangles simultaneously.
- Stores separate hits in `ref (Face, Vector3) back` and `ref (Face, Vector3) front`, allowing tools to prefer the surface nearest the camera or navigate interior geometry.

5. Distance Calculations and Point Occlusion (`HandleUtility.PointIsOccluded`):
- Tests whether a 3D point is occluded by mesh geometry when viewed from `cam`:
  - `Vector3 dir = (cam.transform.position - worldPoint).normalized;`
  - `Ray ray = new Ray(worldPoint + dir * .0001f, dir);` (nudged by 0.0001 units towards camera to avoid self-intersection).
  - `return FaceRaycast(ray, pb, out hit, Vector3.Distance(cam.transform.position, worldPoint), CullingMode.Front);`.
  - If any front-facing triangle is struck between the point and the camera position, returns `true` (occluded).

6. Scene Selection Data Structures (`SelectionPickerSettings.cs`):
- `SceneSelection`: Encapsulates selection state for a single `GameObject` and `ProBuilderMesh`, maintaining `List<int> m_Vertices`, `List<Edge> m_Edges`, and `List<Face> m_Faces` with properties `vertexes`, `edges`, `faces`, and mutation methods `SetSingleFace`, `SetSingleVertex`, `SetSingleEdge`, and `Clear()`.
- `VertexPickerEntry`: Value type struct storing `ProBuilderMesh mesh`, `int vertex`, `float screenDistance`, and `Vector3 worldPosition` for sorting nearest vertices to a mouse click.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, raycasting against mesh faces can be performed using Camera3D.project_ray_origin() and Camera3D.project_ray_normal(). Triangle intersections can be evaluated via Geometry3D.ray_intersects_triangle(). Local coordinate transformations match mesh_node.global_transform.affine_inverse() * world_ray.

sections.heading: DEPTH TESTING
sections.content:
Depth testing governs whether mesh elements obscured by other geometry can be picked. The setting is exposed via `PickerOptions.depthTest` (corresponding to the editor's "Select Hidden" preference toggle).

1. Behavior Modes:
- `depthTest == true` ("Select Hidden" OFF): Only elements directly visible from the camera viewpoint are selectable. Occluded elements are discarded.
- `depthTest == false` ("Select Hidden" ON): All elements falling within the selection boundary are picked regardless of visibility or occlusion by foreground geometry (x-ray picking mode).

2. GPU Offscreen Depth Testing Mechanisms:
- Face Picking Depth Testing:
  - The face picking shader (`BuiltinMaterials.facePickerMaterial` using `Hidden/ProBuilder/FacePicker` or `Hidden/ProBuilder/FacePickerURP`) is configured with `ZTest LEqual`, `ZWrite On`, and `Cull Back`.
  - When rendered to the 16-bit depth buffer (`depthBufferBits = 16`), standard GPU depth buffering discards occluded back/hidden faces.
- Vertex and Edge Depth Testing via Depth Masks:
  - Vertex billboards and edge lines are overlay primitives rendered on top of surfaces.
  - To prevent occluded vertices and edges behind the mesh from rendering into the pick buffer, `GenerateVertexPickingObjects` and `GenerateEdgePickingObjects` generate an auxiliary array of `depthObjects`.
  - For each selected `ProBuilderMesh`, a GameObject named `pb.name + " (Depth Mask)"` is created using the mesh's full triangle geometry `pb.mesh` and `BuiltinMaterials.facePickerMaterial` with uniform `_Tint` set to `Color.black` (`k_Blackf`).
  - The depth mask mesh writes to the Z-buffer with `ZTest LEqual` and `ZWrite On`.
  - Vertex and edge billboards are rendered using `ZTest LEqual`. Elements behind the mesh geometry fail the Z-test against the depth mask and are discarded, or write black pixels (`0x00`).
  - Because valid vertex and edge hash IDs start at `index = 0x02`, black pixels (`k_PickerHashNone = 0x00`) are ignored during CPU decoding.
  - When `depthTest == false`, `depthObjects` is set to `null` and no depth mask GameObjects are instantiated, allowing all vertex billboards and edge lines to render unoccluded.

3. CPU Screen-Space Occlusion Testing:
- For Complete rectangle selection mode, ProBuilder evaluates occlusion on CPU using raycasts via `HandleUtility.PointIsOccluded`:
  - Faces: Occlusion is tested at the arithmetic center of all distinct face vertices: `trs.TransformPoint(Math.Average(positions, face.distinctIndexesInternal))`.
  - Edges: Occlusion is tested at the edge midpoint: `(posA + posB) * 0.5f`.
  - Vertices: When `depthTest == false`, `SelectionPicker.PickVerticesInRect` skips GPU rendering completely and accepts any vertex where `p.z >= cam.nearClipPlane && rect.Contains(p)`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, depth testing during ID buffer rendering can be implemented by setting depth_draw_mode = DEPTH_DRAW_ALWAYS on picking materials and using standard depth testing (DEPTH_TEST_ENABLED). When depth testing is disabled ("Select Hidden"), picking materials set no_depth_test = true.

sections.heading: PERFORMANCE
sections.content:
ProBuilder optimizes picking performance through resolution scaling, temporary texture pooling, bounding-box pixel traversal, and CPU geometric bypass paths.

1. Pick Texture Resolution and Scaling:
- Default resolution matches the camera pixel dimensions: `(int)camera.pixelRect.width` and `(int)camera.pixelRect.height`.
- Support for High-DPI (Retina) scaling via `pixelsPerPoint` (e.g. `EditorGUIUtility.pixelsPerPoint`):
  - `renderTextureWidth = (int)(cam.pixelWidth / pixelsPerPoint)`
  - `renderTextureHeight = (int)(cam.pixelHeight / pixelsPerPoint)`
- Scaling down the render texture reduces fill rate and GPU-to-CPU readback bandwidth by `pixelsPerPoint^2`.

2. RenderTexture Descriptor Configuration:
- Format selection checks supported render texture formats in priority order: `RenderTextureFormat.ARGB32` followed by `RenderTextureFormat.ARGBFloat`.
- `RenderTextureDescriptor` settings:
  - `depthBufferBits = 16`: 16-bit depth buffer.
  - `autoGenerateMips = false` and `useMipMap = false`: Disables mipmap generation.
  - `msaaSamples = 1`, `allowMSAA = false`, `allowHDR = false`: Prevents antialiasing blur and tone-mapping from altering exact integer color encodings.
  - `sRGB = false`: Linear color space ensures exact 8-bit channel bit preservation.
  - `memoryless = RenderTextureMemoryless.None`.

3. Readback and Resource Lifecycle:
- Allocates temporary texture via `RenderTexture.GetTemporary(descriptor)`.
- CPU transfer executes via `Texture2D.ReadPixels(new Rect(0, 0, _width, _height), 0, 0)`.
- `RenderTexture.ReleaseTemporary(rt)` is called immediately after `ReadPixels` to return GPU memory to Unity's pool.
- Extracts pixel array `Color32[] pix = tex.GetPixels32()` and immediately calls `UObject.DestroyImmediate(tex)` to free texture memory.

4. Rect Pixel Scanning Complexity:
- Reading the color buffer does not iterate the entire screen; it bounds iteration strictly to the selection rectangle:
  - `int ox = Math.Max(0, Mathf.FloorToInt(pickerRect.x));`
  - `int oy = Math.Max(0, Mathf.FloorToInt((tex.height - pickerRect.y) - pickerRect.height));`
  - `for (int y = oy; y < Min(oy + height, imageHeight); y++)`
  - `  for (int x = ox; x < Min(ox + width, imageWidth); x++)`
- Processing time scales with the area of the selection rectangle (O(W_rect * H_rect)) rather than screen size.
- `HashSet<uint> used` caches encountered IDs, ensuring `Dictionary.TryGetValue` is executed at most once per unique element in the selection rectangle.

5. Edge Selection Threshold Filtering:
- Edge picking tallies hit counts in `Dictionary<uint, uint> pixelCount`.
- Valid selections require `kvp.Value > k_MinEdgePixelsForValidSelection` (`k_MinEdgePixelsForValidSelection = 1`, meaning at least 2 pixels), eliminating accidental single-pixel hits from line rasterization.

6. CPU Fast-Path Geometric Bypass:
- When `options.depthTest == false` in `PickVerticesInRect`, ProBuilder bypasses offscreen rendering, texture allocation, and CPU readback entirely. It executes direct CPU vertex-in-rect tests, eliminating GPU overhead.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, GPU-to-CPU synchronization can be optimized by fetching only the sub-image corresponding to the selection rectangle via Image.get_region() or using RenderingDevice.texture_get_data() for the sub-rectangle region.

sections.heading: RENDER PIPELINE DIFFERENCES
sections.content:
ProBuilder abstracts render pipeline differences behind the internal interface `SelectionPickerRenderer.ISelectionPickerRenderer`, which specifies `Texture2D RenderLookupTexture(Camera camera, Shader shader, string tag, int width, int height)`. The active implementation is instantiated based on preprocessor symbols and active pipeline checks.

1. Pipeline Detection and Selection (`SelectionPickerRenderer.pickerRenderer`):
- HDRP check: `ShouldUseHDRP()` returns `true` when `HDRP_7_1_0_OR_NEWER` is defined, returning an instance of `SelectionPickerRendererHDRP`.
- URP check: `ShouldUseURP()` returns `true` when `PB_URP_MODE` is defined, returning an instance of `SelectionPickerRendererURP`.
- Built-in Fallback: Otherwise instantiates `SelectionPickerRendererStandard`.

2. Built-in Standard Pipeline (`SelectionPickerRendererStandard`):
- Mechanism: Uses legacy replacement shader rendering via `Camera.RenderWithShader`.
- Camera Configuration:
  - Creates a temporary `GameObject` and attaches `Camera renderCam = go.AddComponent<Camera>()`.
  - Copies camera properties: `renderCam.CopyFrom(camera)`.
  - Sets `renderCam.renderingPath = RenderingPath.Forward`, `renderCam.enabled = false`, `renderCam.clearFlags = CameraClearFlags.SolidColor`, `renderCam.backgroundColor = Color.white`, `renderCam.allowHDR = false`, `renderCam.allowMSAA = false`, `renderCam.forceIntoRenderTexture = true`.
- Pipeline Suppression: Temporarily sets `GraphicsSettings.defaultRenderPipeline = null` and `QualitySettings.renderPipeline = null` to force forward rendering, invokes `renderCam.RenderWithShader(shader, tag)` with tag `"ProBuilderPicker"`, and immediately restores previous pipeline references.
- Reads back pixels into linear `Texture2D` and destroys the temporary camera GameObject.

3. High Definition Render Pipeline (`SelectionPickerRendererHDRP`):
- Mechanism: Uses HDRP custom render callbacks and `HDAdditionalCameraData`.
- Camera Setup:
  - Copies settings to temporary camera GameObject.
  - Attaches `HDAdditionalCameraData hdCamData = go.AddComponent<HDAdditionalCameraData>()`.
  - Sets `hdCamData.flipYMode = HDAdditionalCameraData.FlipYMode.ForceFlipY`.
  - Subscribes `hdCamData.customRender += CustomRenderPass`.
- Custom Render Pass (`CustomRenderPass`):
  - Calls `ctx.SetupCameraProperties(camera.camera)`.
  - Allocates `CommandBuffer cb = new CommandBuffer()` and clears render target: `cb.ClearRenderTarget(true, true, Color.white)`.
  - Retrieves culling parameters via `camera.camera.TryGetCullingParameters(out ScriptableCullingParameters cullParams)`.
  - Performs culling: `CullingResults cullResults = ctx.Cull(ref cullParams)`.
  - Builds `RendererListParams` using `DrawingSettings(new ShaderTagId("Always"), new SortingSettings(camera.camera))` and `FilteringSettings.defaultValue`.
  - Creates renderer list `var list = ctx.CreateRendererList(ref listParams)` and draws via `cb.DrawRendererList(list)`.
  - Submits command buffer: `ctx.ExecuteCommandBuffer(cb); ctx.Submit();`.

4. Universal Render Pipeline (`SelectionPickerRendererURP` and `URPSelectionPickerPass`):
- Mechanism: Uses URP Render Graph API and `ScriptableRenderPass`.
- Request Submission:
  - Allocates temporary `RenderTexture rt`.
  - Prepares `StandardRequest request = new StandardRequest() { destination = rt }`.
  - Subscribes `RenderPipelineManager.beginCameraRendering += CustomRenderPass`.
  - Executes `RenderPipeline.SubmitRenderRequest<StandardRequest>(camera, request)`.
- Custom Pass Enqueueing:
  - In `CustomRenderPass`, creates `URPSelectionPickerPass customPass = new URPSelectionPickerPass(-1)` with `renderPassEvent = RenderPassEvent.AfterRendering`.
  - Enqueues into URP renderer: `camera.GetUniversalAdditionalCameraData().scriptableRenderer.EnqueuePass(customPass)`.
- Render Graph Recording (`URPSelectionPickerPass.RecordRenderGraph`):
  - Adds raster pass: `builder = renderGraph.AddRasterRenderPass<PassData>("ProBuilder Selection Picker Pass", out var passData)`.
  - Configures drawing settings with shader tag `ShaderTagId("ProBuilderPickerA")`.
  - Sets render attachments: `builder.SetRenderAttachment(resourceData.activeColorTexture, 0)` and `builder.SetRenderAttachmentDepth(resourceData.activeDepthTexture, AccessFlags.Write)`.
  - In `ExecutePass`: clears target `context.cmd.ClearRenderTarget(RTClearFlags.Color, Color.white, 1, 0)` and executes `context.cmd.DrawRendererList(data.rendererListHandle)`.
  - Unsubscribes callback upon completion.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, the rendering architecture uses a unified RenderingServer backend with Forward+, Mobile, and Compatibility rendering methods. A single custom shader or Viewport pass can be used across all renderers without needing separate pipeline-specific implementations like Unity's Builtin/URP/HDRP.

cross_references.relationship: ProBuilderMesh core data structures, positionsInternal, facesInternal, sharedVerticesInternal used for geometry extraction
Face, Edge, and SharedVertex representations picked by the renderer
EditorSceneViewPicker and MeshSelection interact with SelectionPicker for user mouse events and selection state updates
Selection modifiers (grow, shrink, loop, ring) operate on element sets returned by SelectionPicker
Overlay and wireframe shaders render visual highlights for picked elements
